chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated him, narrated to us; he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddhal ibn Umar, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'He who claims to be from our Shia while adhering to the rope of others has lied.'

key_terms.عُرْوَة: Rope (metaphor for authority, guidance, or allegiance)

ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for true Shia identity according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s criterion for authentic Shi’ism as exclusive adherence to the Imams’ authority, contrasting it with those who cling to external or rival sources of guidance. This hadith underscores the theological principle of *Wilayah* (guardianship) as the defining mark of the sect, implying that deviation in allegiance constitutes a denial of true Shi’ite identity. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the Shia emphasis on the infallible Imams as the sole interpreters of divine law.

en.badr-shahin: 4. Mohammed bin Ali Majilwayh, May Allah have mercy upon him, narrated to us from his uncle Mohammed bin Abi al-Qasim from Mohammed bin Ali al-Kufi from Mohammed bin Sinan from al-Mufaddhal bin Umar that
Imam as-Sadiq (a) said: "He who claims being one of our Shia while adhering to the rope of others has lied."
